title: mindwalk report
description: LLM-assisted evaluation of one session trace. Findings come from the judge; dimension verdicts are derived mechanically from finding severities so reports stay comparable across runs.

eventCount.description: Event count of the trace the report was generated from; a cheap display signal — freshness is decided by judge.inputDigest

userTurns.description: User-turn count at generation time; with eventCount it lets list badges spot message-only session growth cheaply

model.description: The LLM that actually judged, as reported by the CLI itself; best-effort, display and comparability only — never part of freshness

requestedModel.description: The alias the run was asked for (e.g. "sonnet"), kept so a repeated aliased request can recognize its own cached report

rubricPromptVersion.description: Set only when the report carries a scored rubric; deterministic skips stay fresh across rubric prompt revisions

inputDigest.description: SHA-256 hex of the evidence document the judge read; the report is fresh only while the trace still renders to this digest

verdict.description: max(finding severity), forced to insufficient-data when the trace observability grades the dimension's source signal unavailable

rubric.description: Task-accounting layer: session-specific criteria generated before scoring, grouped by the independent tasks enumerated from the user messages. Optional — a report without it is a dimensions-only report.

reason.description: Why an unavailable rubric is unavailable: transient generation failure, or a deterministic skip a re-run would repeat (no/weak task text, or a conversation-only trace with nothing to cite)

source.description: Rubric generation input mode; cross-agent comparison must only reuse task-sourced rubrics

taskDigest.description: SHA-256 hex over the rendered task wording; a re-evaluation whose digest still matches reuses the rubric unchanged

anchorUserMessages.description: [user #N] ordinals from the evidence document that define this task; validated against the ordinals actually rendered there

anchorSeqs.description: Mark seqs the ordinals resolve to — derived mechanically, never taken from the judge — so the UI can jump to a task's start

coverage.description: What the log let the scorer judge; unverifiability lowers coverage instead of producing warnings

verdict.description: max(finding severity), forced to insufficient-data when coverage is none — computed in Go, never by the judge

note.description: What the scorer felt the rubric did not let it express

evidenceSeqs.description: Event seqs backing the claim; validated against the trace — invalid references are dropped, and a finding with no valid reference left is dropped entirely
